curriculum.lesson_evidence: Sculptures need structure so they stand. Balance means weight is distributed so the piece does not tip. An armature is an inner support (wire, cardboard tube) for softer materials. Test balance early; widen the base or add a counterweight if it wobbles.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
A tall foil figure keeps falling. Give two structural fixes.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: 'Widen and weight the base; add an internal tube armature up the spine.'

WATCH FOR
Adding heavy decoration on top before the base is stable. Structure first, details later.

teach_steps.explain:
Sculptures need structure so they stand. Balance means weight is distributed so the piece does not tip. An armature is an inner support (wire, cardboard tube) for softer materials. Test balance early; widen the base or add a counterweight if it wobbles.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make intentional visual, music, drama or dance choices and name their effect, rather than saying an artwork is simply “nice”. Keep every claim linked to an element or technique.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the elements, techniques or performance choices that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. For movement or instruments, use a clear space, ask an adult to be nearby and stop if anything feels unsafe. You may always describe a choice instead of performing it. One deliberate artistic choice with a named effect is more useful than a longer praise sentence.
